# CoreWeave Cashes in on the AI Gold Rush With a 25% Price Hike, and Customers are Still Lining Up: CRWV Stock Rises 19% (UPDATED)

Editor’s Note: The story has been refreshed with the latest market price action and a revised headline.

CoreWeave Inc.  (NASDAQ: CRWV) raised prices across its artificial intelligence computing offerings in July and is passing along rising hardware costs to customers, as demand continues to accelerate.

## A Quarter of Pricing Power

CFO Nitin Agrawal told analysts on Tuesday’s earnings call that the increase was “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment.”

He added that CoreWeave is separately passing through rising component costs to customers, including pricier GPUs, layering hardware inflation on top of the base price hike.

The company noted that the move was a reflection of the return on investment customers are seeing as they shift more of their workloads toward inference.

Last week, **SanDisk Corp. **(NASDAQ: SNDK) CEO David Goeckeler said AI demand has shifted customer conversations from routine quarterly price negotiations to long-term strategic partnerships, with some of its largest customers already returning to expand multi-year agreements just one quarter after signing them.

results.title: CoreWeave Raised Prices by 25 Percent. Its Near-Term Computing Capacity Is Still Effectively Sold Out
results.author: Georgia Fearn
highlights:
The AI infrastructure shortage is allowing old chips to remain valuable and pushing customers to pay premiums for near-term capacity. 

BY GEORGIA FEARN, EDITORIAL INTERN

Aug 12, 2026

Photo: Getty Images

CoreWeave says its near-term AI computing capacity is effectively sold out. That announcement comes after it raised prices across its product lineup by roughly 25 percent in July.

Rival AI cloud provider Nebius said Wednesday that it could sell its entire 2027 capacity today on terms similar to its latest deals, but it is deliberately holding some back for immediate customer needs. According to the company, shorter contracts can often command even higher prices.

Customers are paying premiums for near-term computing power, new contracts are becoming more profitable, and even older generations of Nvidia GPUs—the chips used to train and run AI models—are still commanding strong prices years after newer chips arrive.

CoreWeave co-founder and CEO Michael Intrator said contracts signed last quarter are expected to carry contribution margins five to 10 percentage points higher than those signed in recent quarters. Customers, he said, are increasingly making money from their AI products and are more willing to pay for the compute that’s needed to grow.

The demand is showing up in CoreWeave’s numbers. Second-quarter revenue more than doubled to $2.58 billion, while revenue backlog reached roughly $104 billion, excluding more than $25 billion of additional commitments signed early in the third quarter.

results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr
- Hyperscaler list prices are far higher: AWS p5 works out to ~$6.88/GPU-hr, Azure ND H100 v5 to ~$12.29/GPU-hr (third-party trackers; not confirmed on primary pages)
- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

## The 2026 price hikes nobody announced

If 2026 were a price war, you would expect a run of press-released cuts. Instead, the documented pricing events of 2026 are mostly increases — several delivered quietly.

CoreWeave — ~25% list-price increase across SKUs (July 2026)

On its Q2 2026 earnings call (August 11, 2026), CoreWeave disclosed “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment,” adding that pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs were “setting new highs” while prior-generation SKUs sat at or above prior levels. Management described near-term capacity as “effectively sold out” (CoreWeave Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Revenue hit $2.58B, up 112% year over year, on a $104B backlog.

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/ ... — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

A 25% across-the-board price hike with continued sold-out capacity is concrete evidence of pricing power in AI compute — even prior-gen GPU fleets are being contracted out to 2029 at attractive prices. This confirms demand still exceeds supply across all GPU generations.

# CoreWeave verhoogt prijzen met 25 procent en is op korte termijn uitverkocht

CoreWeave verhoogde in juli alle SKU-prijzen met ongeveer 25 procent en meldt dat de capaciteit voor de korte termijn uitverkocht is. Ook oudere GPU-generaties worden niet goedkoper meer.

Alisina Nawabi FAQ

## Kort samengevat

- CoreWeave voerde in juli 2026 een prijsverhoging van ongeveer 25 procent door over al zijn SKU's, bevestigde CFO Nitin Agrawal op de kwartaalcall van 11 augustus.
- De capaciteit voor de korte termijn is volgens topman Michael Intrator feitelijk uitverkocht, ook voor oudere Nvidia-generaties; een pas getekend A100-contract loopt door tot in 2029.
- De verhoging raakt nieuwe contracten en verlengingen, niet de prijs van een lopend meerjarig take-or-pay-contract.
- Het is de tweede verhoging in twee maanden bij een grote aanbieder, na de circa 20 procent die AWS per 1 juli 2026 doorvoerde op zijn gereserveerde GPU-blokken.

CoreWeave verhoogde in juli de prijzen van zijn hele productlijn met ongeveer 25 procent, zei financieel directeur Nitin Agrawal dinsdag op de kwartaalcall, terwijl de capaciteit voor de korte termijn uitverkocht blijft.

Wie in Nederland AI-rekenkracht inhuurt, krijgt daarmee de tweede verhoging binnen twee maanden voor de kiezen. AWS trok de tarieven van zijn gereserveerde Nvidia-GPU-blokken per 1 juli al met ongeveer 20 procent omhoog, en CoreWeave gaat er in dezelfde maand overheen. Het tarief is niet het enige dat verandert. De klassieke uitwijk bij dure rekenkracht, een generatie oudere GPU's huren voor minder geld, is bij deze aanbieder dicht.

...

De stap raakt de SKU's: de losse producttypes in het aanbod, telkens een bepaald GPU-type met de opslag, het netwerk en de software eromheen. Agrawal zei dat de margeverbetering van het tweede kwartaal nog van vóór de aanpassing dateert, en dat die aanpassing een verhoging van ongeveer 25 procent over alle SKU's inhield. Als reden noemde hij de vraag in de markt en het rendement dat klanten op hun eigen AI-toepassingen zien nu ze verschuiven van trainen naar inferentie. Gestegen componentprijzen rekent het bedrijf daar bovenop door.

Een lopend contract verandert er niet door. CoreWeave verkoopt capaciteit vooral via meerjarige take-or-pay-afspraken, en die prijs staat vast voor de looptijd. De 25 procent landt op nieuwe contracten en op verlengingen. Volgens Agrawal komt er dit jaar maar een klein deel van de vloot vrij voor herverhuur, maar liggen de gemiddelde verkoopprijzen daarvoor op of boven het niveau van een jaar geleden. De contracten die het bedrijf in het tweede kwartaal tekende, dus nog vóór de verhoging, hadden al een bijdragemarge die 5 tot 10 procentpunt hoger lag dan die van recente kwartalen.

...

Topman Michael Intrator zei op dezelfde call dat de prijzen voor de nieuwste Blackwell- en Vera Rubin-generaties records neerzetten, en dat de tarieven voor eerdere generaties op of boven het niveau van jaren geleden liggen. Ook van die oudere generaties is CoreWeave naar eigen zeggen grotendeels uitverkocht. Als voorbeeld noemde Intrator een pas getekend contract voor A100-capaciteit dat doorloopt tot in 2029. Die architectuur stamt uit 2020.

De verhoging landt in een markt waarin de klant weinig te kiezen heeft. Intrator zei dat de capaciteit voor de korte termijn feitelijk is uitverkocht, waardoor het bedrijf contracten op steeds gunstiger voorwaarden kan sluiten. Beleggers lazen dat als kracht: het aandeel steeg woensdag ruim 19 procent. Voor elke GPU die in gebruik wordt genomen melden zich volgens de directie meerdere klanten, en de capaciteit gaat bewust naar de contracten die CoreWeave strategisch belangrijk vindt.

results.title: CoreWeave Tests The Limits Of Cloud Pricing - TalkMarkets
results.author: Jimmy Copell
highlights:
The standard worry about renting out computing power is that it eventually becomes a commodity business. You buy expensive servers, you rent them out, and over time your margins get squeezed between rising hardware costs and customers demanding cheaper rates. CoreWeave CRWV is showing that the current artificial intelligence infrastructure market is behaving differently. The company raised prices across its cloud offerings by about 25% in July as near term capacity remained effectively sold out, while also saying it is passing through higher component costs. That is meaningful evidence of pricing power today. The open question is whether that power lasts once supply catches up and customers have more alternatives.

...

### What happened 

CoreWeave disclosed on its August earnings call that it raised prices across its cloud offerings by about 25% in July. Management said the move reflected the current demand environment and the improving returns customers are seeing as more workloads shift to inference. Separately, customers have reportedly been told that prices for some Nvidia based artificial intelligence server systems shipping early next year will rise by more than 15%. Nvidia has not publicly confirmed those increases.
